summary: LinkedIn came back online in a big way this month. Impressions jumped to 1,983 (from 11 in April when posts were held for the Cancun launch) and you added 11 new followers, your strongest follower growth in the last four months. The clear winner was your Fairmont Austin thank-you post, a warm first-person recap of the Iron Chef night with Katie Kent and Joshua Jensen. It out-performed every designed piece we ran. The takeaway is simple: your audience responds to your voice and your relationships, not polished templates. Website traffic softened to 82 sessions as April's Cancun launch bump normalized. Organic search settled at 18 sessions, still above the March baseline of 14 but below April's 24. Behind the scenes we built you a custom RFP tool (in your hands for review), rolled out your new Corporate Travel Lead title across your email signatures, updated your phone number on the site, and scoped the app proposal.

findings.title: Your Voice Out-Performs Polished Design
findings.description: The top post of the month was your Fairmont Austin thank-you recap, a single first-person post tagging Katie Kent and Joshua Jensen. It beat both the designed Costa Rica carousel and the Cancun blog repost. The takeaway: warm, in-the-room posts about real relationships are the strongest engagement driver for your audience right now. We'll lean into that format.

findings.title: LinkedIn Is Back and Growing
findings.description: Impressions went from 11 in April to 1,983 in May, and followers climbed by 11, your biggest monthly gain in four months. The Cancun carousels finally going live plus the Fairmont post restored reach and pulled in new people. The engagement rate settled at 4.4%, which is healthy at this new volume.

findings.title: Website Settled After April's Cancun Bump
findings.description: April hit 111 sessions on the back of the two new Cancun blogs and a 71% jump in organic search. May normalized to 82 sessions with organic at 18, still above the March baseline of 14 but below April's 24. The expected pattern after a content launch. The next destination cycle is what keeps this curve climbing.
